core_obligations: Show that (1) implies (2), using the existence of a diagram with U -> X surjective (proof lines 4343-4345).
Assume two diagrams as in the statement with U -> X surjective and h having P, and build the double diagram of U <- U x_X U' -> U' over V <- V x_Y V' -> V' (proof lines 4346-4371).
Apply the source-and-target descent characterization to lift P to (h, h') and then, because U x_X U' -> U' is surjective, to descend P to h', concluding (2) implies (1) (proof lines 4372-4376).
For representable X and Y, apply the same characterization to identify (1) and (2) with f having P, and treat the case of representable f with a base change and fppf local P (proof lines 4379-4404).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a property P of morphisms of schemes which is etale local on the source-and-target, and a morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, it is equivalent to require that h has P for every commutative diagram with etale vertical arrows from schemes U, V or for a single such diagram with U -> X surjective; when X and Y are representable this is equivalent to f having P, and when P is also preserved under base change and fppf local on the base it agrees with the representable sense (source lines 4313-4340). The proof of (2) implies (1) is the substance: from one diagram with U -> X surjective it builds the double diagram U <- U x_X U' -> U' over V <- V x_Y V' -> V' and applies the descent characterization of source-and-target local properties twice, once to lift P to the pair (h, h') and once to descend it to h' along the surjective U x_X U' -> U'.
